newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul raises foreign shareholding limit to 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: Seoul raises foreign shareholding limit to 23 pct.

text.p: South Korea will raise the ceiling on foreign shareownership to 23 percent of a listed company from the current 20 percent, effective from May 1, the finance ministry said on Monday.
The ownership ceiling for a foreign individual in a listed company would be raised to six percent from the current five percent, a ministry statement said.
It also said the total foreign ownership limit on Korea Electric Power Corp and Pohang Iron and Steel Co will rise to 18 percent from the current 15 percent.
South Korea has more restricted foreign ownership of the two "strategically important" companies.
A foreign individual's ownership in the two firms will continue to be limited at one percent, the statement said.
